engagement_title: Summit & Sable marketplace relaunch: pull a field and bench mess of recovery gear to one honest look, give every SKU a compliant plain ground primary that also survives on the charcoal, introduce a second webbing colourway without a reshoot, and stand up the storefront graphics package
vertical: E-commerce and retail: a value band recovery and overlanding gear brand in Boulder, Colorado, relaunching a nine SKU range on a marketplace and on its own storefront
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork post quoted in the ledger for an ongoing e-commerce editor to make existing product photos consistent and to swap colours on specific parts of a product, with the client's own verbatim bar preserved: without ruining the original image, the lighting, shadows and textures must remain completely natural, and sloppy masking, flat colours or unrealistic edits cannot be accepted. The real post names no client, so the brand is laundered to the coined fictional label Summit & Sable and no real marketplace, retailer, person or trademark appears anywhere. Co-anchor: the Freelancer.com Modern Store Graphics Package brief, in which a small online shop refreshing its storefront asked for a hero banner sized for desktop AND mobile, product detail image assets plus iconography, and section and decoration graphics tying the pages together, with clean lines, bold but balanced colour, plenty of negative space, nothing fussy as the stated art direction, and asked explicitly for layered source files PLUS labelled optimised exports so the team can swap copy and images later. That last request is honoured literally here, because the authored source is delivered alongside the editable document rather than in place of it. The storefront platform is laundered to a generic online storefront.
client_one_liner: Our shots are half clean bench packshots and half gritty tailgate frames, the marketplace will not take a primary with anything in the frame, and we are launching a second webbing colour we are not paying to reshoot.
client_brief:
Summit & Sable, spring relaunch

We make recovery straps, soft shackles and overlanding kit. Nine SKUs, thirty five to two hundred and twenty dollars. Our buyer is somebody with a lifted truck and a budget, and he is buying because the gear looks like it works, not because it looks expensive.

Our pictures are two different jobs stapled together. Half are bench packshots on a pale sweep from the day we listed. Half are field frames a friend shot off a tailgate in low sun with dust in the air. Both look fine on their own. Side by side on a page they are two brands. Pull the whole range to one look.

The marketplace primary is the thing that keeps failing us. Nothing in the frame but the product on a plain ground: no logo, no words, no dirt, no scene. Square. Our own storefront is the opposite: there the field frames are what sells, our mark is allowed, and everything sits on our charcoal.

We also want one detail crop per SKU, wide, showing the stitching and the hardware finish, because that is the argument for paying our price instead of the cheap import.

The part we care most about. We are launching the same strap in a second webbing colour, Ridge Blue, and we are not paying to shoot the range again. We have sent a photograph of the spool so you can see the colour. This has to look like a photograph of a blue strap. If the weave goes flat, or the shadow inside the coil goes wrong, or it looks painted on, it is worse than not doing it.

Then the storefront itself: a hero for desktop and a hero for mobile, a set of small spec icons, a band that ties the sections together. Clean lines, bold but balanced, plenty of space, nothing fussy. Send the editable file and the labelled exports so we can swap copy later.

And a note saying what you did to each shot.
price_band_and_audience: Value band recovery and overlanding gear at thirty five to two hundred and twenty dollars, buyer twenty five to fifty, off-road and 4x4 owners buying on rugged credibility and price. The band is load-bearing and it cuts against the obvious instinct: the correct look here is honest, bright, hard-wearing and legible, flat daylight on the primaries and unstyled dust on the secondaries, with type that reads as workwear signage rather than as a lifestyle magazine. The same nine SKUs at a nine hundred dollar premium expedition band would correctly be shot dark and cinematic, low key, warm rim light, heavy blacks, tiny type in a lot of black space, and shipping that treatment here reads as pretending and prices the brand out of its own buyer's search results. Push the other way into hard flash, saturated orange and shouting sale-shaped graphics and it drops below its band into disposable import territory, which is exactly the comparison the detail crops exist to win. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even with every technical gate green. A posted job of this shape runs 800 to 2,000 dollars fixed, or an ongoing retainer.

brand_identity.tagline: Gear that looks like it works.
brand_identity.sector: E-commerce and retail, value-band recovery and overlanding gear
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2019 in Boulder, Colorado. Small owner-run shop, under ten people, selling on a marketplace and its own storefront.
brand_identity.about: We make recovery straps, soft shackles and overlanding kit for people with a lifted truck and a real budget. Nine SKUs from 35 to 220 dollars. Our buyer is not paying for a name, he is paying because the gear looks like it will hold when he is stuck at dusk on a fire road. The detail is the whole argument: the stitching and the hardware finish are what separate us from the cheap import sitting next to us in search results.
brand_identity.audience: Off-road and 4x4 owners aged 25 to 50, buying on rugged credibility and price. They trust flat daylight and visible workmanship and they distrust anything that looks staged or expensive.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Value band, 35 to 220 dollars. The look is bright, hard-wearing and legible, honest daylight on the plain-ground shots and unstyled dust on the field shots. Never premium-expedition cinematic, never discount-banner loud. Either extreme reads as pretending and loses the buyer.
brand_identity.typography: Type should read as workwear signage: a sturdy condensed or grotesque for headlines and spec callouts, a clean neutral text face for body and the range table. Bold but balanced, plenty of negative space, nothing magazine-like.
brand_identity.voice: Blunt and plain. We say what the gear does and what it is rated for. Certified working loads are stated as certified and never rounded or dressed up.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The only brand mark file we can find is a flat screen-size export our old developer left us, plus a photo of the same mark on a woven label. We have no scalable artwork and no written guidelines. Charcoal is our storefront ground and Ridge Blue is the new webbing colour we are introducing. Treat the notes above as direction, not a locked system.
brand_identity.values: Honesty in the picture and the spec. Durability over shine. Fair price for real capability. If an edit would make the product look like something it is not, we would rather it stayed plain.

assets_supplied.name: summit_bench_packshots/ (9 frames, 5472 x 3648)
assets_supplied.kind: Bench packshots, one SKU per frame, pale grey sweep, even studio light, shot the day the range was listed.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The clean ones. Every SKU is in here at least once."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three SKUs are soft shackles and sewn-loop straps whose eyes are genuine holes through the product, and a one-call knockout returns a cutout that looks complete while leaving those eyes filled with the captured sweep, which is invisible against a plain near-white ground and reads as a grey plug the moment the same cutout is placed on the brand's charcoal or over a field frame. The anodised shackle bodies also sit distinctly cooler than everything else on the bench.

assets_supplied.name: summit_field_frames/ (11 frames)
assets_supplied.kind: Field frames shot off a tailgate and on a trail in low sun with dust in the air, gear in use.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The ones that actually sell it. Shot by a friend, late afternoon, dusty."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two frames have the sunlit dust cloud clipped to nothing, so a highlight recovery on them returns an image in which visibly nothing has moved, at full success, and there is no signal distinguishing that from a recovery that worked. The low sun also puts a strong warm cast on the webbing specifically, so the frame-wide correction that fixes the scene pushes the strap colour away from the bench version of the same SKU.

assets_supplied.name: summit_ridge_blue_spool.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Photograph of the new webbing on the spool, sent as the colour reference for the second colourway.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "This is Ridge Blue. This is the colour it has to be."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The new colour sits close to opposite the current webbing on the colour wheel, which is a distance a hue move does not reach; the correction runs, reports success, and returns a flat, desaturated, slightly wrong blue, and pushing it further destroys the weave the client explicitly refuses to lose.

assets_supplied.name: summit_mark_export.png
assets_supplied.kind: A flat screen size export of the brand mark, a wordmark with a small ridge device, supplied as the only mark file the brand can find.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our logo. It is the file our old developer gave us."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is far below the size the desktop hero needs, so it can only be placed by being enlarged unless it is rebuilt as geometry, and what looks like a transparent file is a white card baked in behind the mark, which is invisible until it lands on the charcoal.

assets_supplied.name: summit_label_photo.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Photograph of the same mark screen printed on a woven webbing label sewn to a strap.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The same logo, on our label. Better quality than the file, we think."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Naming the label returns the label rather than the print, and the screen print sits down in the weave so the strokes break up along the warp, which does not show at the size the photograph is viewed at.

assets_supplied.name: summit_range.csv
assets_supplied.kind: One row per SKU: name, working load, webbing width and length, hardware, finish, warranty line, price, and which colourways it ships in.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The range as we list it. The working load numbers are certified, so they cannot be changed or rounded."

acceptance_bar: The client's own bar, verbatim and binding: the lighting, shadows and textures must remain completely natural, and sloppy masking, flat colours or unrealistic edits are rejected outright regardless of what else passes.

The second colourway reads as a photograph of a strap in that colour, with the weave, the shadow inside the coil and the sheen on the webbing all still present and still behaving as one light. A flat area of colour sitting where a strap used to be is a fail even if the hue is right.

Laid together the way a category page lays them, the bench sources and the field sources read as one brand: one white point, one black point, one contrast behaviour, one colour for the same webbing in both.
Every marketplace primary sits on a plain ground with nothing else in the frame at all: no mark, no words, no dirt, no scene, square, at or above the intake minimum.
Where a product has a hole through it, the hole is a hole. Cutouts are judged on the brand charcoal and over a field frame, not only on the plain ground.
No delivered file exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions and no crop record in the run carries an enlargement entry, the mark included. A mark placed at hero size by being enlarged fails.
Each SKU has one wide detail crop that actually contains the stitching and the hardware it is supposed to show, rather than a crop that merely fills the frame.

The mark used on the storefront is placeable scalable artwork with a genuinely transparent ground: a real viewBox present, no opaque full-canvas rectangle riding underneath, and no white card behind it on the charcoal.

The storefront package is one working file carrying the desktop hero, the mobile hero, the two secondary tile canvases and the section band, each keeping its own canvas size, with live retypeable text, every photograph actually present on every canvas, and the spec icons arriving as editable vector rather than as pictures.
The labelled exports are delivered alongside the editable file and the self contained source it was authored from, named so the client can tell which asset is which without opening them.
One type system across every canvas, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the actual weight used.

The note states per source what was applied and how the field treatment differed from the bench treatment, every resize any tool reported, and an honest account of what the second colourway can and cannot be made to do.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, counting image_vectorize here rather than as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_apply_preset, image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_fill_area, image_remove_background (transparent and backgroundColor routes), image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs, detection_confidence, upscale_factor), image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: The whole of the picture work: bringing two source families to one house look a frame at a time, confining the corrections that must not touch the scene, building the second colourway as a masked, region confined move that keeps the weave and the shadow, isolating nine SKUs onto a plain ground including three whose eyes are holes, cutting the square primaries and the wide detail crops without enlarging anything, and rebuilding the brand mark as geometry off the better of the two supplied sources.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The storefront graphics package as one native editable document carrying five roots at five canvas sizes, which is the only surface here that composes free-form fixed canvas layout. The spec icons are authored as inline vector so they arrive editable, every photograph is carried as image data because a reference renders as an empty box at full success, family and weight are declared per text element, and each root declares its own canvas so the desktop and mobile heroes do not collapse to one size.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: One type system across the heroes, the tiles, the band and the handover. The recommender will not pair for you, so the pairing is the agent's art direction and has to land on workwear legibility at a value band rather than on expedition-brand austerity or sale-shaped shouting. Numeric weights are non-standard per family, names must be laundered into canonical form before the kit call, and the CSS has to use the returned slug or the whole page falls back silently.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock plus Adobe Boards, counted as one surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (entityScope StockAsset, short query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the one frame the brand does not own, a dust and trail texture for the section band, IP clean and at genuine camera scale with generative-tech candidates excluded, then graded into the house look rather than dropped in as bought. The Boards half persists the selects the client signs off from, placed within the per call cap, a partial result read as partial.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching a pixel.
trajectory.judgement: Primaries, secondaries, detail crops and the colourway are raster work against a hard intake spec; the storefront package has to be authored because the client asked explicitly for a file they can swap copy in later. The brief pins both destinations.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming a surface per deliverable and the confirmed tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role and its SKU.
trajectory.judgement: Twenty sources across two families plus two mark files plus a colour reference; the manifest is what stops a field frame being treated as a bench frame twelve steps later.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by SKU and by source family.

trajectory.action: Preview all twenty frames, both mark files and the spool reference, and triage: which SKUs have both a bench and a field frame, which field frames have lost their highlight entirely, which products have holes through them, how far the new colourway sits from the current webbing, and which mark file is a flat export and which is a photograph of a print.
trajectory.judgement: The two mark files look interchangeable and need opposite treatments, and the two source families need one destination reached by two different routes. Counting files is not the same as reading them.
trajectory.produces: A per frame and per asset triage note, including a first read on how far the colourway has to travel.

trajectory.action: Straighten the field frames shot off the tailgate, before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop, and the wide detail crops have no margin to give away.
trajectory.produces: Levelled field masters, bench frames untouched.

trajectory.action: Fix one house look and bring both families to it one frame at a time, recording the parameters applied, and decide per clipped frame what to do when a recovery returns an image in which nothing has moved.
trajectory.judgement: Bench and field are two lighting worlds and one batched parameter set is exactly wrong for that. Where the highlight is genuinely gone there is nothing to recover, and the honest move is to reframe or to name the frame rather than to keep pushing.
trajectory.produces: Twenty graded masters at source scale with a per frame parameter log and a note on the frames that could not be brought all the way.

trajectory.action: Confine the corrections that break the scene when applied whole-frame, selecting the webbing and the anodised hardware by their own material properties rather than by the product they belong to.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the whole gate: naming the strap pulls the selection to the strap and naming the tailgate pulls it to the truck. The warm cast is on the webbing, not on the picture, so the correction has to be too, or the same SKU ends up two colours across the two families.
trajectory.produces: Corrected frames where a whole-frame move would have cooled the dust or flattened the scene.

trajectory.action: Build the second colourway as a region confined move on the webbing only, judged by eye against the spool photograph and against the weave and coil shadow it must not lose.
trajectory.judgement: This is the deliverable the client says is worth more than the rest of the job, and the client's bar is about naturalness rather than about hue accuracy. Confinement is not optional and neither is looking at the weave afterwards.
trajectory.produces: A second colourway per affected SKU, with the parameters applied recorded, judged beside the reference.

trajectory.action: Isolate the nine bench masters onto the marketplace's plain ground and to transparent variants for the charcoal tiles, reading every returned tradeoff record rather than the success message.
trajectory.judgement: The intake forbids anything in the frame but the product, and the storefront wants the opposite ground from the same master. Three SKUs are products with holes through them, which is a different topology from a solid object.
trajectory.produces: Nine plain ground plates and nine transparent variants, each with its tradeoff record captured.

trajectory.action: Cut the square marketplace primaries at the intake size and the wide detail crop per SKU on the stitching and hardware, reading the confidence and bounds each crop returns and never reaching a size by enlargement.
trajectory.judgement: A detail crop has to contain the argument, not merely be wide, and a subject aware crop on a long thin strap against a pale sweep has very little contrast to find. Optical centring on a shackle with an offset pin is not geometric centring.
trajectory.produces: Nine primaries at spec and nine wide detail crops with their confidence readings recorded.

trajectory.action: Cut the branded field tiles at one to one and four to five from the graded field frames, where the mark is permitted and the scene is the point.
trajectory.judgement: These are the opposite deliverable to the primaries and they must still be the same brand: same webbing colour, same black point, same honesty about dust.
trajectory.produces: A field lifestyle tile set at both ratios, matched to the primaries.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for a dust and trail texture for the section band, filter to photography, exclude generative-tech results, license and download at full resolution, then grade it into the house look.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose existing light can be brought to the house look rather than the best thumbnail, and keep it plain enough to sit behind type without competing with the gear.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP clean, camera scale frame graded into the set.

trajectory.action: Rebuild the mark as geometry, triaging the two supplied sources: the flat export takes a selection, a polarity flip and a trace, while the photographed label needs an ink level prompt naming the print's own properties or it returns the label. Inject a viewBox and remove the opaque ground path, then judge both candidates at the size they actually reproduce.
trajectory.judgement: Two look-alike inputs needing opposite treatments, and the better looking source is not necessarily the better artwork: a print sitting down in a weave breaks up along the warp at trace level, which the photograph does not show at viewing size.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent mark chosen between two candidates on evidence.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's, judged against a value band buyer who reads workwear signage as credible and magazine typography as pretending. Weight cannot be inferred from a style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML with five roots at five canvas sizes (desktop hero, mobile hero, the two secondary tile ratios and the section band), carry every photograph as image data, author the spec icons as inline vector inside explicitly sized top-left anchored wrappers, place the rebuilt mark as inline vector, and declare family and weight on every text element, then upload the file and hold the returned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a reference is not a photograph, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override collapses a mixed size set. The design work is holding clean lines and real negative space at a value band without letting it drift into expedition austerity.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML carrying the whole storefront package, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at the first canvas, and parse the returned per canvas markup for the other four.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition only ever shows the first artboard, so four of the five canvases can be checked no other way.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document, an inspected first canvas, and a per canvas markup audit for the rest.

trajectory.action: Create the selects board, add the graded set, the colourway variants and the licensed frame within the per call placement cap, re-sending only the entries the response names as failed.
trajectory.judgement: A partial success is reported as success, and vector is not boardable, so the mark and the icons belong in the handover instead of on the board.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped.

trajectory.action: Name and package the labelled export set beside the editable document and the source, and write the note.
trajectory.judgement: The client asked for labelled exports so the team can swap things later, which means the naming is a deliverable and not housekeeping. The note owes them an honest account of the colourway rather than a claim that it was achieved.
trajectory.produces: A labelled export set, the source, and a written handover covering per source treatment, every reported resize, and the colourway finding.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the colour the client named can be reached at all on this material. The correction runs, reports success and returns a strap that is blue, so there is no error, no warning and nothing in any response that distinguishes a move that landed from one that ran out of range. What only appears when the result is set beside the spool photograph is that a hue move of this distance does not arrive: the webbing comes back desaturated and a shade away, reading as a flat colour laid over a strap rather than as a strap in that colour, which is precisely the outcome the client wrote their acceptance line to forbid. Pushing the same move further does close the hue gap and takes the weave and the coil shadow with it, and that too reports success.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter prevents it, because the distance between the current webbing and the named colour is a fact about two physical materials that no tool reports and that the spool photograph alone does not settle. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says the brand is launching a second colourway and will not reshoot, and the acceptance line about naturalness is the client's standing requirement rather than a warning about range. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the answer is a different construction, building the colourway as a confined move plus a tonal rebuild rather than as a single hue shift, and possibly a different answer entirely, which is telling the client which of the two colourways can be shown honestly and which needs a shoot.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-plan the colourway as a confined, multi-part build on the webbing selection alone, re-judge the weave and the coil shadow at full resolution rather than at preview scale after each attempt, re-do every SKU that shares that webbing so the range does not carry two different blues, and write the limit into the handover rather than shipping a flat strap and hoping.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A relaunch whose headline new product is a photograph of a strap with a flat blue rectangle where the weave was, delivered against an acceptance line that names that exact outcome as unacceptable, on a range whose entire price argument is that the gear looks like it works.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the isolated products are actually isolated. Three of the nine SKUs are soft shackles and sewn-loop straps whose eyes are open holes through the product, and a subject knockout has no way to punch an enclosed interior: it returns a cutout that is clean at the outer edge, complete looking and entirely convincing, with the eye quietly filled by the captured pale sweep. On the marketplace's plain near-white ground that fill is invisible, so the primary passes. The same cutout on the brand charcoal, and again over a field frame in the secondary tiles, shows a grey plug sitting in the middle of a hole. Nothing in the response distinguishes those three frames from the six solid ones.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering does not dodge it, because the defect is a property of the product's topology rather than of the sequence, and it is legible only on the second ground, which is a deliverable rather than a diagnostic. (b) Nothing states it: the brief lists the SKUs and says the primary must be on a plain ground, which is the intake rule, not a disclosure about holes. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the correct route is a different chain, selecting the sweep as a material so the selection reaches through the eye, inverting it, and filling, rather than asking a subject detector for a product.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-judge every cutout on the charcoal and over a field frame rather than on the plain ground, re-derive the three affected SKUs through a material-named sweep selection inverted and filled so the eye stays open, and re-cut both the primary and the charcoal tile from the corrected master so the two grounds do not disagree.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Nine primaries that pass intake and a storefront whose hero tiles show the brand's own soft shackles with their eyes plugged grey, which reads to this buyer as a fake product photograph on exactly the SKUs that carry the highest margin.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer treats the two heroes, which were authored differently for good reasons. The desktop hero puts the product to one side with real negative space, so the photograph is placed as an image element and survives. The mobile hero is a full bleed crop with type over it, which is naturally authored as a panel carrying the photograph behind its content, and that construction is discarded outright: the panel arrives as an empty box with correct geometry and no picture, at full success and with no warning of any kind. The document's rendition shows the first canvas only, and the first canvas is the desktop hero, which looks exactly right. The returned per canvas markup is the only channel in which the mobile hero, the two tile canvases and the section band exist at all.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Doing it right the first time presumes knowing which of two ordinary ways of putting a photograph on a canvas survives this importer, which no response reports and no checklist enumerates, and no ordering changes it because the drop happens at import and the import is the last step. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for a desktop hero and a mobile hero and for negative space, which is art direction. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the fix re-authors the canvas around a different construction, an image element sized and positioned to bleed with the type placed over it, which changes how the whole mobile composition is built.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-author every canvas that carries a full bleed photograph around an image element rather than a panel, re-check the same markup for the other things that silently do not survive, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export, and audit all five canvases from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A storefront package delivered as an editable file in which the mobile hero, which is where most of this buyer's traffic actually lands, is an empty box with a headline floating on it, having reported success throughout and having previewed perfectly on the one canvas anybody looked at.

deliverables.name: Summit & Sable range masters, field and bench, plus detail crops
deliverables.spec: Twenty masters brought across two source families to one house look (one white point, one black point, one contrast behaviour, and the same webbing colour for the same SKU in both families), plus one wide detail crop per SKU that actually contains the stitching and the hardware finish, plus one licensed camera scale trail frame graded into the same world. Every output at or below its source pixel dimensions with its tradeoff record captured, and a per frame parameter log naming which frames could not be brought all the way and why.

deliverables.name: Summit & Sable Ridge Blue colourway
deliverables.spec: The second webbing colourway produced on the existing photography as a region confined build, with the weave, the sheen and the shadow inside the coil intact and behaving as one light, judged by eye against the supplied spool reference and delivered across every SKU that shares that webbing so the range carries one blue rather than several. Delivered with the parameters applied and with an honest written statement of how far the colour could be taken and what a reshoot would buy.

deliverables.name: Summit & Sable marketplace primaries and charcoal tiles
deliverables.spec: Nine square marketplace primaries at intake size on a plain ground with nothing else in the frame, plus nine genuinely transparent variants used on the brand charcoal and over field grounds, both cut from the same graded master. Where a product has a hole through it the hole is transparent, and every cutout is judged on the charcoal and over a field frame rather than on the plain ground. One set with one cut logic, not one picture at several sizes.

deliverables.name: Summit & Sable mark and spec icon system
deliverables.spec: The brand mark rebuilt as placeable scalable geometry chosen on evidence between a flat screen size export and a photograph of the screen printed label, with a real viewBox present, no opaque full-canvas rectangle riding underneath and no baked white card behind it on the charcoal, placeable at hero size without ever being enlarged. decision_gates: Which deliverables are raster work and which need an authored fixed canvas document, given that only one surface composes free-form layout.
Where to put the house look, given that the correct answer for this band is honest daylight legibility rather than the cinematic treatment the category's premium brands use.
What to do with a field frame whose highlight is genuinely gone, when a recovery returns an image in which nothing has moved.
Whether the warm cast belongs to the picture or to the webbing, and therefore whether the correction is frame wide or confined.
How to build a colourway the client will accept, and when to say that the distance cannot be crossed honestly on this material.
Knockout route per SKU: a subject route for the solid products versus a material-named sweep selection inverted and filled for the three whose eyes are holes.
Which ground a cutout is judged on, given that one of the two grounds hides the defect the other reveals.
Which of the two supplied mark files becomes the artwork, judged at reproduction size rather than at viewing size, and how to word the selection on the one that is a photograph of a print.
Whether to trust a confident crop on a long thin strap against a pale sweep, or to spend the extra calls on an explicit selection.
How a full bleed photograph is constructed on a canvas, and how each canvas beyond the first is verified when only the first can be looked at.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a value band buyer plus the real numeric weight per family.
How the labelled exports are named, given that the client asked for them specifically so somebody else can swap things later.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of recovery straps. IDENTITY: these are this brand's actual nine SKUs with their actual certified working loads, their actual hardware and their actual stitching, and the detail crops exist precisely to prove the physical product is not the cheap import, so a regenerated strap defeats the entire commission. The second colourway is a change to an existing photograph of an existing product, not an invention of a new one, and the client's acceptance line says so in their own words. SPEC: the marketplace intake demands a plain ground with nothing else in frame, square, above a minimum size and with no interpolated pixels, while the storefront demands the opposite ground from the same master, and a hole through a product must remain a hole; none of that is satisfiable or checkable in a generated image. EDITABILITY: the client asked explicitly for the file plus labelled exports so their own team can swap copy later, which is a definition of the deliverable, not a preference. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did this colour move actually land, did this cutout leave the eye open, did this canvas keep its photograph.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), four surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, apply_preset, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, select_subject, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and detection_confidence, fill_area, remove_background in both the transparent and backgroundColor forms, and vectorize are all verified headless across 27 live calls, and alpha is verified to survive both crops at png with feathered partial-alpha pixels preserved. The checkpoints rest on documented live findings rather than assumptions: masked hue moves are verified to work at moderate distance while a near-complementary swing to a named colour is documented as out of reach, so the recolour ceiling is real; remove_background is verified NOT to punch an enclosed interior, returning a solid opaque region where a hole should be; and the importer is verified to drop a panel carrying its photograph as a background while an image element survives, at HTTP success with no warning, with the document rendition documented as first artboard only. Material selection by prompt is verified (a wood plank field returned with an object cut out of it), which is what makes the sweep-through-the-eye route real. The mark triage rests on the verified prompt asymmetry between naming a substrate and naming the ink's own properties, plus the verified missing viewBox and opaque path zero. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, inline SVG becomes native editable vector shapes, the product is a genuine editable dcx findable by asset_search, and external image references resolve to placeholders so every photograph is inlined and the payload is routed by uploaded URL. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit verified end to end including non-standard numeric weights and slug-reached display cuts. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed, a real full resolution licensed JPEG, boards persisting with a 12 placement cap and partial success returned as success. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no InDesign claim of any kind, no vector render or vector merge, no upscaling, no compositing, no OCR, no text-to-image, no generative fill, no background replace by prompt, no image placed into an Express template, no fill_text, no animate_design, no batch above 20.
